claims.text: Containerless electromagnetic levitation combined with drop calorimetry, fast-response pyrometry, and high-speed imaging will enable accurate and efficient in-situ determination of melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, and volume change in selected HEAs.
High-purity CoCrFeMnNi and derivative HEAs can be prepared for these measurements by standard casting and homogenization.
An electromagnetic levitation apparatus can be integrated with drop calorimetry, fast-response pyrometry, and high-speed video to capture rapid melting events.
The experiments can be conducted under argon or vacuum.
Temperature ramp rates of 10^2 to 10^3 K/s are suitable for the proposed measurements.
Containerless melting measurements can use spherical samples with diameters of 2–3 mm.
High-speed radiative images and calorimetric heat-flow traces can mark melting onset, phase transitions, and volumetric expansion.
Electromagnetic levitation creates a containerless environment.
The containerless environment prevents extraneous nucleation and contamination.
Synchronized calorimetric and radiative measurements directly correlate fusion energy with structural changes and volume expansion during melting.
Melting temperatures will be measured to within ±1–2% accuracy.
Latent heat and entropy of fusion can be derived from distinct calorimetric plateaus and sharp thermal transitions.
Volume change at melting will be quantified with an error within ±2%.
Radiative imaging and diffraction markers can provide simultaneous validation of melting-related structural transitions.
Traditional DSC and container-dependent calorimetry often suffer systematic errors caused by container interactions.
The methodology is primarily applicable to medium-temperature HEAs such as CoCrFeMnNi and selected derivatives.
Application to refractory HEAs may require modification of the levitation and measurement systems.
Synchronization, temperature calibration, and data acquisition remain uncertain for very rapid melting events.
The approach is to be rejected if melting temperature differs from expected values by more than ±2%, no clear latent-heat plateau appears, or imaging lacks consistent structural-transition markers.

contradictions.description: The initial material is specified as a conventionally cast and homogenized solid HEA, whereas the validation experiment specifies lyophilized CoCrFeMnNi samples. No preparation route connecting these materially different sample states is provided.
